2  THIS MFA CROB IN MFA NO.903/16 PASSED U/O.41 RULE 22 OF CPC, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 10.08.2015 PASSED IN MVC NO.
1000/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT, SRIRANGAPATNA, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT FOR COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL AND MFA CROB., COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal and cross-objection, both the insurance company and the petitioner have challenged the judgment dated 10.08.2015 passed in MVC.1000/2012 by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Srirangapatna.
2. The parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. Brief facts of the case are on 17.03.2012 at about 10.15 p.m. on Bannuru-Srirangapatna road near Chikkapalya gate, the husband of the petitioner by name Mayikrishnegowda-the deceased, met with NC: 2023:KHC:41003 an accident while he was pillion rider in the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA11-V-8540 rided by his son Mr.D.M.Avinasha, hit by another motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-11-U-5595 (offending motor cycle) he was treated at Columbia Asia Hospital, Mysore, Apollo BGS Hospital, JSS Hospital, Mysore but he was succumbed to death on 24.03.2012.
The petitioner being the dependant moved the tribunal seeking grant of compensation of Rs.28 lakhs.
Claim was opposed by the both owner and the insurer of the offending motor cycle.
The tribunal after taking the evidence, by the impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.12,25,819/- with 9% interest.

Aggrieved by the same, the insurance company has filed MFA No.903/2016, pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement the petitioner has filed the MFA.Crob.No.85/2016 on various grounds.
NC: 2023:KHC:41003 4.

Heard the argument of Sri.O.Mahesh, learned counsel for the insurance Company, Sri.Sreenivas V, learned counsel for petitioner and Sri.M.Y.Sreenivasan, learned counsel for owner of the motorcycle.
5.
It is the contention of learned counsel for the insurance company that there is involvement of two motorcycles, the motorcycle in which the deceased was traveling is not made as a party.
Rider of the offending motor cycle is not made as a party.
Petition is of non-joinder of necessary parties.
There is a contributory negligence on the part of the son of the deceased.
The deceased was aged 50 years, no future prospects is to be added.

The tribunal has taken 15% future prospects, the deceased has left The Divisional Manager vs C.K. Latha on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187914749/
3

behind sole serving dependant, 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses instead of 1/3rd,
and the interest awarded at 9% is higher side and he sought for modification.
NC: 2023:KHC:41003 6.
Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the deceased was aged 50 years at the time of accident.
He was an agriculturist by profession.
The petitioner has produced Exs.P.14 to P.21-RTC extracts to show the land owned by the deceased.
Exs. P.22
to 25 stone quarry license owned by the deceased, who was earning not less than 15,000/- per month.
Income assessed at Rs.7,000/- by the tribunal is at lower side and he sought for enhancement.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both the parties and perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, injury sustained by the deceased and his death on account of the injuries.

The rider of the motorcycle in which the deceased was travelling has set the law into motion by filing the complaint to the police and after investigation, NC:
2023:KHC:41003 charge sheet was laid against the rider of the offending motor cycle.

9. The contention of Sri.O.Mahesh, is that the rider has been acquitted of the charges, there is contributory negligence on the part of Mr.Avinash, the son of the deceased and this has not been considered by the tribunal.
10. Exs.P.1 to 5 are the prosecution papers.
Ex.P.2 is the crime detail form which gives dimension how the accident had taken place.

It is pertinent to note that the width of the road is 20 ft at the place of the accident, on extreme left side of the road, the motorcycle was moving, the offending motorcycle came behind and hit against the motorcycle which was going ahead.
There is no evidence on record to show that the motorcycle of the deceased was stopped or taking turn when the accident took place.
Hence, there is no scope for contributory negligence as contended by the insurance company.
When there NC: 2023:KHC:41003 is no contributory negligence, the question of son of the petitioner and deceased is necessary party has no substance.
The owner of the offending motorcycle is duly represented, the insurance policy is in force, the rider of the offending motor cycle is also not a necessary party.
11. The deceased was an agriculturist and a businessman by profession.
Exs.P.14 to 25 goes to show he was cultivating 4 acres 18 guntas of wet lands
Exs . P.22

to 25 is license issued by the Senior Scientist, Mines and Geology Department, Mandya, that the deceased was also doing stone quarry for supplying of stones for building constructions in an extent of 3 acres of land in Sy.No.185 of Andrahalli Village, Srirangapatna Taluk.
This shows the potential income of the deceased.
The tribunal has assessed Rs.7,000/- as income as that the deceased was a person with no proof of income.
In the year 2012, a person with no proof of income is assessed NC: 2023:KHC:41003 at Rs.7,000/- in the Lok Adalat.
Here in this case, the deceased is owning 4 acres 18 guntas of agricultural land and also doing stone quarry in 3 acres of land.
He is earning sufficiently, he cannot be compared as a person with no proof of income.

Hence, the income assessed at Rs.7,000/- is The Divisional Manager vs C.K. Latha on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187914749/
4 inadequate and it shall not be less than Rs.8000/-.
Accordingly, the income is assessed for the purpose of calculation.

12. The assessment of compensation in a case of this nature has been settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgment rendered in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED -VS- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS, so also the selection of multiplier in SARLA VARMA (SMT.) AND OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED -VS- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: SARLA VARMA (SMT.) AND OTHERS VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By applying the said principles, the compensation has to be determined.
Undisputedly, the deceased was given treatment at Major Hospitals at Mysore and a sum of Rs.2,63,723/- has been spent by the petitioner which requires to be reimbursed.
As the deceased was aged '50' years, the future prospectus has to be taken at 10% instead of 15% assessed by the tribunal.
Applicable multiplier is '13'.
All these aspects are taken into consideration loss of dependency is Rs.8000 + 800 (10%) = Rs.8800-2933(1000)=5867 x 12 x 13 =9,15,252/-.
Under conventional head 'loss of consortium' to the wife at Rs.20,000/, funeral and loss of estate at Rs.10,000/- each has to be assessed.
Then the total compensation including the medical expenses comes to Rs.12,18,975/- as against Rs.12,25,819/- awarded by the tribunal which is in excess of Rs.6844/-.
Since the difference of the enhancement is only is 0.5%, it is not proper to interfere with the award of the tribunal.

Adverting to the argument of insurance company regarding rate of interest is concerned, there is no reason assigned by the tribunal in awarding interest at 9% except relying upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Municipal Corporation of Delhi Vs. Association of Victims of Uphaar Tragedy reported in 2011(14) SCC 481.

entities.text: Municipal Corporation of Delhi Vs. Association of Victims of Uphaar Tragedy reported in 2011(14) SCC 481
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is a distinction in award of interest in Uphaar Tragedy's case is a theater accident which is different to that of this nature.
An accident cannot be a windfall for the petitioner nor a peanut, it should be a just compensation.
15. In the year 2012, no Banks will offer interest @ 9% on the fixed deposit.

In this regard, the Division Bench of this Court has made an elaborate discussion in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and Ors. -vs- Venkateshan.V. and Ors. in M.F.A.No.5896/2018 c/w M.F.A.Nos.4444/2018 and 4659/2018 (MV) DD 24.08.2020 with reference to - 12 - The Divisional Manager vs C.K. Latha on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187914749/
5 NC: 2023:KHC:41003 Section 149(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Rule 253 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and Section 34 of Civil Procedure Code, wherein at Para 52 has laid down principles.

It reads thus:
"52.Thus, under Section 34 of CPC being squarely applicable to the interest awarded by the tribunal and Section 34 empowering the tribunal to award pendente lite interest and discretion being vested with the Court/Tribunal to award interest from the date of suit or petition is to the maximum extent of 6% p.a. or in other words, not exceeding 6% p.a., the contention raised by the learned Advocates appearing for the Insurance Company deserves to be accepted and accordingly, it is accepted.
16. As seen from the catena of decisions, only in the cases where special reasons are recorded, higher rate of interest is awarded.
Here in this case, the Tribunal has not assigned any reason for awarding higher rate of interest.
The interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% per annum is not comparable to prevailing Bank rate of interest at relevant point of time.
Hence 6% interest is to be awarded in the facts and circumstances of this case.
In view of the above discussions, both the appeal as well as the cross objection merits consideration.

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER a) MFA.No.903/2016 filed by the Insurance Company is allowed in part.
b) MFA.Crob.No.85/2016 filed by the petitioner is allowed in part.
c) Order of the Tribunal in awarding compensation of Rs.12,25,819/- is maintained.

d) The insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation at 6% interest from the date of petition till the date of deposit within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
e) The amount in deposit shall be  transmitted to the Tribunal.

Sd/-
